notes_context:
These notes were distilled from earlier work in this repository that passed verification. Follow them unless the code or CHANGELOG.md shows they no longer hold.
- [at-0001] Round money only with round_money: Always round monetary results with ledgerly.money.round_money (half-up to the cent); never use Python's round() or a bare Decimal.quantize(), which use banker's rounding and produce wrong invoice totals.
  (learned from task E01 on ledgerly 1.0.0; relied on 1x, 1 passed, 0 failed)
- [at-0002] Normalize money via to_money and round_money: Convert any incoming amount with to_money() and store it rounded with round_money() from ledgerly/money.py; compare against ZERO rather than a literal Decimal.
  (learned from task E02 on ledgerly 1.0.0; relied on 0x, 0 passed, 0 failed)
- [at-0003] Raise BillingError with snake_case codes: Reject invalid input by raising BillingError(code, detail) from ledgerly/errors.py with snake_case codes such as "invalid_state", "invalid_quantity" and "negative_amount".
  (learned from task E02 on ledgerly 1.0.0; relied on 0x, 0 passed, 0 failed)
- [at-0004] Exclude bool when validating integers: When validating an integer argument, reject bool explicitly with isinstance(x, bool) before the int check, since True/False pass isinstance(x, int).
  (learned from task E02 on ledgerly 1.0.0; relied on 0x, 0 passed, 0 failed)

item.title: Normalize datetimes with ensure_utc before arithmetic
item.content: In ledgerly, always pass incoming datetimes through `ledgerly.clock.ensure_utc` before comparing or doing arithmetic (see `current_period` in `ledgerly/subscriptions.py`); never compare raw `started_at`/`after` values directly.

candidate.title: Compute periods via floor division on timedelta
candidate.content: Compute billing period boundaries the same way as `current_period` in `ledgerly/subscriptions.py`: `n = (at - start) // length` then `start + n * length`, using `timedelta(days=sub.period_days)` as the period length.
